title: Icons in icons only task manager reduce to unusable size when Panel is filled up with other widgets
line: On a crowded panel, Task Manager icons keep their full size and the tasks can be scrolled with the mouse wheel instead of shrinking to tiny dots.
explanation: Tasks in a horizontal panel had no minimum width, so when the panel gave the Task Manager only its minimum size (one task wide) every task was squeezed to fit, leaving icons a few pixels wide. Vertical task lists had a minimum but simply overflowed past the widget. Each task now keeps at least its full icon size; when the tasks don't fit, the list is clipped and scrolls with the mouse wheel or touchpad inside the Task Manager, so the panel layout itself is unchanged (unlike the reverted scrollable-panel change). Drag-and-drop hit testing now maps through the scroll offset.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: scroll tasks instead of shrinking them to nothing

When the panel was crowded, tasks kept shrinking with no lower limit and
their icons became too small to use. Tasks now keep at least their full
icon size, and the task list scrolls with the wheel when it overflows.

BUG: 447603

media.caption: Master: panel crowded with Global Menu and 9 clocks, the Task Manager's five tasks are squeezed into tiny dots.
With the fix: same panel, the Task Manager shows tasks at full icon size.
With the fix: the mouse wheel scrolls through all the tasks in the crowded Task Manager.

review.text: Direction follows the VDG conclusion (Task Manager scrolls, panel unchanged) and the minimum task width plus clipping are reasonable; the mapToItem change also simplifies the RTL hit test. But scrolled-out tasks are invisible with no hint: a newly opened or activated window can be off screen, and while overflowing the wheel silently stops doing what the user configured (cycle tasks). Maintainers will expect those handled before this lands.
changes: Scroll the active task (and newly added tasks / demands-attention tasks) into view (positionViewAtIndex-style ensureVisible).
Add some overflow cue (fade or scroll indicator) at the clipped edge.
Don't silently override the 'wheel cycles through tasks' setting: e.g. only take over the wheel when wheelEnabled is None, or use horizontal/Shift scrolling, and explain the choice in the MR.
